translation:
...the five deities beyond (Niranjan, the primal power [Adya Shakti], Brahmaji, Vishnu, and Shankarji) run the kingdom. All the world worships, bows to, praises, and performs yajnas and homas for them. Because of this, no soul can pass from their ocean-of-existence-like kingdom into the ocean of bliss (the supreme abode) — that is, no soul can escape their grip. (Register No. 2078, p. 124.)

Niranjan (Dharmaraya) obtained the kingdom of the three worlds (the ocean of existence) from God by performing austerities (Register No. 2078, p. 80). Through the power of his austerities he became arrogant, so he was punished: in future he would not have the Lord's darshan; each day he would devour one lakh souls and create one and a quarter lakh souls. Such was the curse Niranjan received (Register No. 2078, p. 16). Niranjan forcibly demanded from Karma-Kachhap (the Tortoise of Karma) the materials for building the three worlds, the ocean of existence (Register No. 2097, p. 92). Ritualists (karmakandis) hold that Niranjan received a curse, so that his head was cut off — God cut it off, that is, rejected him. For this reason the saints and Harijans (devotees) do not accept Niranjan; but the ritualists believe that Niranjan, by his own authority, does not let souls leaving the ocean of existence pass beyond him. So they take the coconut as the symbol of Niranjan: taking a pot as his torso, placing on it leaves of creation such as mango and ashopalav [a decorative tree] as if they were his limbs, and setting a coconut on those leaves as Niranjan's head, they imagine Niranjan's body in this way and worship it, accepting it thus in auspicious ceremonies. But the Harijan saint-devotees, having taken refuge in God, have no need to flatter or serve Niranjan.

_Kabir ind trisama bhagka, bhalka chhuta ek,
tin tin lok mariya, varpar nahi chhek ||4||_
(Kabir: out of the whole cosmic egg one strand out of thirty parts broke loose, and it struck down all three worlds; the destruction it wrought has no end.)

Das Kabirji says: out of the whole cosmic egg of the Perfect Parabrahma, one strand out of thirty parts broke loose, and through it the threefold-gunas maya struck down all three worlds; the destruction it has wrought has no end.

In the Samagam, among Kabir's sakhis, in the Bij anga, in Anga sakhi 15, he says:

_kabir bund athah jalhar, thak mag kachhu nahi,
ind trisame bhagme, sab jag upji vilay ||14||_
(Kabir: the drops of this cosmic egg are like a boundless, fathomless lake; from one thirtieth part of this egg the birth and destruction of all this world takes place.)

Das Kabirji says: the drops of this cosmic egg are like a lake without shore or bottom — their extent cannot be estimated. From one such thirtieth part of this cosmic egg, the birth and destruction of this entire world takes place.

Revered Yadunath writes, in Litiyu no. 92, p. 105, that is, that a single spark flew out from a great blazing fire.

||Kedaro||
_tis bhan ek thaur dekhe, mai tis bhan ek thaur,
ta upar ek chand biraje, yathe chhabi nahi aur ||tek||
dharan so gagan gagan so dharani, ta par kiyo vistar,
kot kot arun bhari shobha, bin ravi bhayo ujas ||1||
hai nirgun sargun bhayo sagar, ta par adhik bhar,
bas jaye sur tihare darasaki, pandit arath vichar ||2||_
(O mother, I have seen the light of thirty suns falling in a single place; above it sits a moon, and there is no beauty greater than this. His form spans from earth to sky and from sky to earth, spread over both; his splendor has become like the reddish glow of crores upon crores of suns, so that his light shines forth even without the sun. He is the Absolute beyond gunas, yet he has become a vast ocean of qualified, embodied being besides — O scholars, reflect and consider the meaning of this.)

Surdasji says: O Mother (Radha), I have seen the form of God, radiant as if the light of thirty suns fell in a single place. Above that form a moon sits. No other form in the world can surpass it. His form extends from the earth to the sky and from the sky to the earth; his brilliance has thus spread over both earth and sky. His splendor has become like the glow of ten million suns' reddish dawn-light, so that his light shines forth even without the sun. Though he is, in this way, the Parabrahma Paramatma beyond the gunas, he has yet become like a vast ocean of qualified, embodied (saguna-sakar) form, and depends greatly on that embodied aspect. Surdas says: it is my wish that a vision of your form of this kind should become fixed in my mind. O scholars, consider and reflect on what this form must be like.

_kula jat kubharki, chapna ghadchan tris,
nam kiya shri ramka, tansaran banyan tris_
(The potter's caste is by nature like a creator: he made thirty small clay saucers, and gave, as their maker, God's — Shri Ram's — own name; and as he went on shaping those small saucers, they grew as large as great platters of Ram.)

The potter's caste is by nature like a creator. He made thirty small clay saucers (chappan), and as their maker was given God's, Nature's, own name; and while he went on making these small saucers, they grew as large as great platters of Ram.

Kabirji has regarded the Id-Anda (cosmic egg) as maya; he wrote of it in the Id-Maya anga (chapter).

_kabir adhar ind ajmal hai, adhar kare vepar,
kala sankeli saiya, tab sab ekakar ||5||_
(Kabir: the divine Id, unfathomable and wondrous, conducts its affairs suspended in space without support; when the Lord withdraws his device, all this creation becomes one.)

Das Kabirji says: the divine Id (cosmic egg), the Lord, is unfathomable — exceedingly beautiful, strange, and wondrous. It conducts its affairs suspended in space, without any support or prop. When it withdraws and shuts down its device and power, all this creation merges into a single form.

Krishna went with Arjuna to fetch back the Brahmin's children who had been carried off; showing who that Parabrahma was who carried the children away, and why, Jivandasji has described him in the sakhis above, and, explaining it, said: that same enchanting flute-player, the Lord who is Namdev and Kabirji's God, who came to Dwarka and rose to the children's rescue, is one and the same; and the Lord of the world's cosmic egg who carried off the Brahmin's children is, in his original form, that very same Lord. For this reason the names of Brahma are: Omkar, 1. Brahma, 2. Mansa Devi, 3. Jyot Swaroop (form of light), 4. Vishnu Gun, 5. Hiranyagarbha, 6. Tej (radiance), 7. Gudhi, 8. Mahakali, 9. Niranjan, 10. Gayatri, 11. Id, 12. Mahatattva — these are the names of Brahma. That is, he is the Lord of the cosmic egg, while the enchanting flute-player is the Lord of infinite crores of cosmic eggs.

Inquiring students of the Samagam who have made copies of it have, in them, noted down the Vallabh Sampraday's view of this supreme reality as follows. Vallabhi Gosainji Hararayji, in his Shikshapatra, page 38, gives a fairly full explanation: 1. the Lord of the imperishable abode, 2. the cosmic form of the unmanifest Brahma [Akshar Brahma], 3. Rama together with Vaikuntha's Lakshmi. In this way the Vallabh Sampraday has described the nature of God under three aspects.

Kabirji, however, has said that this reality has become known under twelve names, and that these twelve names belong to Brahma, that is, to maya (Kuvarpura Handwritten Manuscript No. 1, page 135; also Panchratnamala, Anga 3, page 660, verse 4). There too Kabir says: _maya brahm bhinna mat jano_ (know Maya-Brahma to be a separate doctrine).

_kabir jar darpan nirmal liya, jine dekha agam apar,
jau deu maya muchchha, to pragat na hoy didar_
(Kabir: the Harijans took up a mirror-clean inner faculty, free of maya's stain, and beheld the boundless reality no sense can know; but were I to make this embodied Brahma-maya swoon senseless, how could I then see the divine reality at all?)

Das Kabirji says: the Harijans (devotees) took up a mirror-like inner faculty (antahkaran), free of the stain of maya, and with it beheld the boundless divine reality that cannot be known through the senses. But if I were to make this saguna-sakar (qualified, embodied) Brahma-maya swoon and lose consciousness, then how could I see the divine reality at all? This is mentioned in Krishnadas's Parachari Charam, pages 44–45.

_bar namki prasiddhi kari, sab sansar soi ur dhari ||544||
chaud lok tahe the bhaye, koy sant yati vichitra bhaye ||545||_
(He made the twelve names well known, and the whole world took them to heart; from them the fourteen worlds came to be, and some saints and ascetics turned out without real substance.)

Because the true understanding of the illusory world that God created was not grasped, people of the path of knowledge — the followers of the six systems of philosophy — declared, according to their own understanding, that Brahma-maya should be understood through twelve names, and all the people of the world took this to heart. From this divine reality of twelve names the fourteen worlds/realms came to be, and some saints and ascetics turned out to be without real substance or truth.

_kabir bara nam pare, kiya rai lon,
jisahi chalave panth tun, tisahi bhulave kaun ||3||_
(Kabir: he made the twelve-named reality regal and beautiful; O Lord, whomever you lead in whatever way, who then can mislead him and stop him?)

Das Kabirji says: to conceal his true nature, and to lead unwise people into confusion about him, God, through these twelve names, made this twelve-named reality appear regal, supreme, and beautiful. O Lord, whomever you lead, and however you lead him — who then can mislead and stop that one from following it?

_kabir bar ang sakarka, bar ank nirakar,
bare ang niranjani, aur avastha char ||22||_
(Kabir: the embodied aspect of the divine reality has twelve parts, and the formless aspect too has twelve parts; but all these twenty-four parts, and the body's four states besides, are portions of the Nirguna Brahma.)

Das Kabirji says, in the Bij-swara Anga: the divine reality's saguna-sakar (qualified, embodied) aspect has twelve parts, and the nirguna-nirakar (unqualified, formless) aspect also has twelve parts; but all these twelve-and-twelve parts, together with the body's four states, are portions of the Nirguna Brahma.

In this way Kabir has referred, in two sakhis, to the twelve names of Brahma-Maya (Id).

Parvati desired to see the form of Vasudevji, but no one is capable of seeing it. In a second episode, Parvati asked: "Mahadevji, what is the nature of your Vasudevji's form?" Rudra replied: "Look at the sun's form — it is truly the form of the Purusha, but because of its extreme brilliance it appears in the shape of a disc; that is only a portion of maya. If you wish to see his true form, you must give up maya and, in proper union, look toward the indwelling Self (Antaryami Atma) seated in the heart — giving up infatuation with maya, possessiveness, pride, impurity, anger, greed, lust, betrayal of trust, addictions, and wrongdoing, and, with the senses mastered and a calm disposition, through the power of pure feeling. The saints and Harijans (devotees) are able to see him in this way. If, instead of the fleshly eye's fleshly sight, you look at the Self in the form of the solar orb, you will see the formless-and-formed [nirakar-sakar] form of your own chosen deity (Ishtadev), and attain supreme contentment." Hearing this, Umiyaji (Parvati) said, "Make my sight pure."

Hearing this, Mahadevji uttered the name of Ram, placed his hand on her head, and firmly established her mental meditation. Because of this she first saw the sun's form, though incompletely — seeing the sun's crown upon its head, earrings in its ears, its chest adorned and filled from every pore with many garlands of splendor, and its extremely radiant hands, feet, body, and lustre, she felt very great joy. Then she said to Mahadevji: "O Lord, I understand it to be so that your Govindji's form cannot be seen with sight — I have understood this much, but now describe it and tell me." Rudra said: "Umiya, listen — let me tell you the form of my Lord. The brilliance of this sun is but the twenty-first part of the radiance of the nail of the little toe of Vasudevji's blessed foot. That is why the sun does not come fully into your sight — so how could you possibly be capable of knowing Govindji?"

_namo narayanadastu sarasaya mahatmane,
vishuddhagyanavikshyaya kotisuryasamarchishe ||71||_
(Salutations to Narayana, the delightful great soul, who can be seen only through purified knowledge, and whose splendor is like that of ten million suns.)

Salutations be to Narayana, the delightful great soul, who can be seen only through purified knowledge and whose splendor is like that of ten million suns.

Umiya said: "O Lord, I have understood Vasudev just as you have described him. The form of Govindji, whose lotus feet hold the splendor of infinite crores of suns, cannot be seen by me; therefore I have today come to know that Govindji as being of the nature of light (Jyoti Swaroop)."

_kabir parbrahmke tejka, kaisa hai unman,
kahevekee shobha nahi, dekha hi praman ||1||_
(Kabir: no estimate can be given of the radiance of Parabrahma Paramatma; there is no worth in describing its splendor — only by seeing it can one know what it is like.)

Das Kabirji says: what the radiance of Parabrahma Paramatma is like — no estimate or inference of it can be given. There is no worth in describing and telling of its splendor; only by seeing it with one's own eyes can one know what it is like.

_kabir dekhya ek agam hi, mahima kaha nav jay,
tej bund parasmani, nayane rahya samay ||2||_
(Kabir: I have seen the one profound reality; its glory cannot be described — a single drop of its radiance is as magnificent as the touchstone, and it has come to dwell in my eyes.)

Das Kabirji says: I have seen the one profound divine reality; its glory cannot be described. A single drop of its radiance is as magnificent as the touchstone (Parasmani), and it has come to dwell in my eyes.

So how could that Vasudev come within the sight of this world? (Now, the ascertainment of Brahma.) For this reason foolish people take it that Brahma is of the nature of light, and radiant only; but he does in fact possess form. Like a tortoise, he too has withdrawn his senses, and for this reason (some holy men call Brahma) formless. But when one considers from what place these senses, the three gunas, and the five elements have developed, one will understand that such is the nature of his true, essential form. Having known this, one should give up the distinction between formed and formless and remain absorbed only in one's own devotion (bhajan) — so said Mahadevji. Hearing this, it occurred to Parvatiji's mind that, since God is embodied (sakar), one ought to become a worthy, qualified person to see him, because without the darshan of Shri Krishna one cannot attain happiness; and since she had not attained that darshan at this time, she wondered what to do, and began forming devotional reflections in her mind: "If he were not embodied, how could he have taken away the Brahmin's sons without hands, how could he have come to Dwarka without feet, how could he have spoken to Arjuna without a mouth? And if Parabrahma had no eyes, how could he have seen Shri Krishna? And if he had no mouth, how could he express an opinion, and how could he have said to Shri Krishna, 'By my power of maya I have summoned this Brahmin's son here, in order to bring you here'? And how did it come about that, beholding Vasudev, Shri Krishna, the great yogi and teacher of the Gita scripture, prayed to his own embodied form?"

For that Parabrahma has the activity of all the senses, yet he does not come into anyone's vision unless full qualification (adhikar) is attained. He who has, within merely one thirtieth part of a single portion of himself, fashioned the whole cosmic egg — the sun and moon, the moving and unmoving universe, the nine planets, the garland of constellations, yoga, maya, and all else — even so, what people describe is only the radiant form arising from his powers. The remaining twenty-nine parts remain intact, and no one's sight can reach them; therefore people go on saying of him, "He is light, he is light." It is only because they fail to attain the direct experience of his embodied nature that they call him formless — for if there were no form at all, the very word "formless" could not arise.

Only through the grace of the Merciful Lord (Kripanath) does one gain the benefit of attaining his darshan; therefore one should simply keep remembering his name, so that through his grace we shall gain the benefit of his darshan. Just as a farmer, in order to store grain, keeps aside a moshitu (moshayo — the clean grain that falls below when winnowing grain in a sieve), so the Merciful Lord has, within his own true light — that which is called Nirguna — tied up and set aside that portion called Brahma as his moshitu. From one part of it the Merciful Lord did, as it were, the farming of the cosmic egg, and has kept the remaining twenty-nine parts tied up as the moshitu.

Such is the immense capability of Shri Krishna, the flute-holding Lord. Who, without his grace, can know that Govindji, who upon each single hair of Vasudevji's body has fashioned crores upon crores of Virats (cosmic forms), and within every single pore of each of those Virats there dwell countless cosmic eggs. Heaven, the mortal world, and the netherworld — these three worlds together form a single Virat form. Here Surdasji bears witness. (A kirtan follows.)

(Raag Sarang) ||Malgodi||

_chosi sarup jagannath jagat guru, jagat pati jagadish,
jog jag jap tap vrat dulambh, pyare lalso grahe gokul ish ||tek||_
(That Lord of supremely excellent form, guru and master of the world, the lord of the universe, unattainable through yoga, sacrifice, japa, austerity, or vow — that beloved darling, Lord of Gokul.)

_jake jathar trailokya jala thal, panch tattva chaukhan,
balak hoi jhulat bij palane, pyarelal jashomati bhovan nidhan ||2||_
(In whose belly rest the waters and lands of the three worlds, the four quarters made of the five elements — that same one, having become a child, swings in the cradle; O beloved darling, treasure of Yashomati's house.)

_ek ek rom kot vairat tan, anant kot brahmand,
lie ochhang mat jashoda, pyarelal apne nij bhuj dand ||3||_
(On every single hair of his cosmic body dwell endless crores of cosmic eggs; yet mother Yashoda takes the beloved darling onto her lap, and lifts him up in her own arms.)

_anurin shravata sudharas pancham, chintamanisi dhen,
vai taji jashomatiko pay pive, pyare lala bhagatanku sukh den ||4||_
(Though the wish-fulfilling cow ever yields sweet nectar, leaving that aside, the beloved darling, giver of joy to his devotees, drinks the milk from Yashomati's breast.)

_ravishashi kot kala bamb lochan, trividhi tap mir jat,
anjan det het sut ve chakh, pyarelal lekar kajal mat ||5||_
(His wide eyes hold the splendor of crores of suns and moons, by whose power even the threefold afflictions are removed; the mother, out of love, applies kohl to those eyes of her beloved darling son.)

_kshiti map tripad gunit karunamay, bal chhali diyo re patal,
dehori olang sakat nahi so prabhu, pyarelal khelat nandjike dwara ||6||_
(The merciful one who, measuring the earth in three strides, deceived King Bali and pressed him into the netherworld — a Lord whose threshold none can cross — that same beloved darling plays at Nandji's door.)

_kamalanayak vaikunthsayak, sukh dukh jake hath,
khandh kambal kar lakuti nagna pad, pyarelal bandhe hai nandjiki rani ||8||_
(The lotus-eyed Lord, the resort of Vaikuntha, in whose hand lies the power to give happiness and sorrow, a blanket on his shoulder and a staff in hand, going about barefoot — that beloved darling, for stealing butter, is bound fast by Nandji's queen, Yashoda.)

_ved vadat upanishad khat ras, urpe bhagata nahi,
gopi gop povalki mandalime, pyarelal hasi hasi juthan le khat ||9||_
(The Vedas, Upanishads, and the six systems of philosophy speak of him at great length, yet devotion to him is not in their hearts; while the company of gopis, gopas, and cowherd boys laughingly and joyfully eat the beloved darling's leftover food.)

_baka baki bakasur sakat trinavat, agh dhen vrishbhas,
kans keshiku gat dini, pyare lal rakhe hai charan nivas ||10||_
(Having slain Baka, Bakasur, Shakatasura, Trinavarta, Aghasura, Dhenukasura, Vrishabhasura, Kansa, and Keshi, and delivered them, the beloved darling has granted them abode at his own feet.)

_bhagat vachhalo prabhu patit odharan, rahe sakal bharpur,
marag rok padyo hath dware, pyarelal patit shiromani sur ||11||_
(The Lord, loving to his devotees, deliverer of the fallen, remains fully present everywhere; O beloved darling, I, Surdas, the greatest sinner among sinners, stand blocking your path, fallen at your very door.)

Surdasji says: what great merit these residents of Vraj must have, that even the great Brahmaji speaks of them in a spirit of devotion — of that supremely excellent Lord of radiant form, the greatest guru of the world, the master of the world, whom one cannot attain through yoga, sacrifice, japa, austerity, or vow, that beloved Lord who is the God of Gokul; in whose belly rest the waters and lands of the three worlds and the four quarters made of the five elements, and who, having taken the form of a child, swings in the cradle. O beloved Lord, you are the treasure-house of Yashodaji's home. In every single pore of this cosmic (Virat) Lord's body dwell endless crores of cosmic eggs; yet that very one Yashodaji plays with in her lap, and lifts up the dear, beloved Lord in her own arms. For that Lord the wish-fulfilling cow always yields sweet, delightful nectar; yet leaving that aside, the beloved Lord, for the happiness of his devotees, drinks the milk from Yashodaji's breast. The radiance of his eyes exceeds that of crores of suns and moons combined; by its power even the threefold afflictions are removed. His mother, for the good of her dear, beloved son, takes kohl and applies it to those excellent eyes. Counting three strides and measuring the earth, he deceived King Bali and pressed him down into the netherworld; no one can withstand the force of such a mighty Lord — yet that same dear, beloved Lord plays in Nandji's courtyard. The beloved husband of Lakshmiji, the resort of Vaikuntha, in whose hand lies the power to give happiness and sorrow — with a blanket on his shoulder and a staff in his hand, barefoot, the beloved Lord goes about. This Lord is the doer and sustainer of his devotees; his vow is to nourish the world. Because butter was stolen from his head [i.e., he was caught stealing butter], the beloved Lord was bound by Nandji's queen, Yashodaji. The Vedas, Upanishads, and the six systems of philosophy speak a great deal, yet in their hearts there is no devotion toward this Lord; while the company of gopis, gopas, and cowherd boys eat this beloved Lord's leftover food, laughing with joy. Having slain Bakasura, Shakatasura, Trinavarta, Aghasura, Dhenukasura, Vrishabhasura, Kansa, Keshi, and others, he delivered them, and this same beloved Lord granted them a place at his own feet. Such a Lord, gracious to his devotees, deliverer of sinners, remains fully present everywhere. O beloved Lord, I, Surdas, the greatest sinner among sinners, stand blocking your path, holding fast at your door.

Such is Vasudev, who dwells in the hearts of the Harijans (devotees).

_kabir mor mugat pankaj nayan, kundal makrakar,
so murat mere nayan baso, chitme karat bihar ||2||_
(Kabir: may that form — wearing a crown of peacock feathers, lotus-petal eyes, fish-shaped earrings — dwell in my eyes and move joyfully in my mind.)

Das Kabirji says: may the form of the Lord Shri Krishna — who wears a crown of peacock feathers, whose eyes are like lotus petals, and who wears fish-shaped earrings — dwell and remain in my eyes, and move about in joy and delight within my mind.

Vaishnav Jivandasji said that the Lord's greatness and majesty come into no one's sight except a Harijan's; and if such a one beholds him with love, it becomes a source of great auspiciousness and well-being — that is, one attains the fulfillment of human birth and comes to a state of supreme bliss (paramanand) whose very nature is love.

(Raag Sorath)

_santo bhai re ulajhan bhari, pathafer — achraj ek bau bhari,
kahat sunat kachhu samaj na aave, avigatki gat nyari, santo ||1||
koi kahai ham nirgun sove, par nirgunka gun kaisa,
koi nirgun koi sirgun (kahavat) bhai, ye (vame mohi) bada andesha ||san||2||
nirgun kahiyo nam mahatam, sirgun santa biraje,
nirgun sirgun ek rup hai, koi ek nij jan nirkhai,
pani pavan bhaya jab mela, tab ek rup hoi barkhai ||san||4||
(shabd surati jab doy milave, tabahi amirasa barse ho ||)
kahat kabir antarki karni, pragat hoy tab sachi,
apne piyajike sukh karan, nagan magan hoi nache ||san||5||_
(O saints, brothers, a great tangle has arisen — a great wonder in this variant reading; nothing can be understood by speaking of it or hearing of it, so strange is the way of that unmanifest one. Someone says, 'we dwell on the Nirguna' — but what special quality does the Nirguna have? Some call him Nirguna and some Saguna, brother, and this raises great doubt in me. The Nirguna is called the glory of the Name, while in Saguna form he is present among the saints; Nirguna and Saguna are one and the same form, and only a rare soul beholds this himself — when water and air come together in union, then it rains down as one single form. When the Word and one's inner attention (surat) meet, then the nectar-rain falls. Kabir says: the working of one's inner devotion becomes true only once it is made manifest; for the sake of one's own beloved's joy, one becomes lost and immersed, and dances in ecstasy.)

Das Kabirji says: O saints, a great tangle has arisen — no understanding of it comes whether by speaking of it or by hearing of it; such is this strange matter of the eternal divine reality. Someone says, "We worship the Nirguna (attributeless) reality" — but what special quality can the Nirguna reality have? Ah, friend, some call him Nirguna and some call him Saguna, but this raises a great doubt in me. For the greatness of God's Name itself is called God's Nirguna aspect, while in the form of the saint he is present and shines forth in Saguna form. The Nirguna reality cannot be understood without any shape, form, or manner whatsoever, and yet whenever any form comes before it, that Nirguna reality withdraws and moves away. But when a meeting takes place between Nirguna and Saguna, the two together take on a single form and rain down as grace; when the Word — God's Name — and one's inner attention (surat) meet, then the nectar-essence of this divine reality rains down. Das Kabirji says: it is genuine only when such a feeling awakens in the working of one's own inner disposition — like a bride's dispositions becoming guileless, joyful, and absorbed, rising up in eagerness, in order to please and gladden her husband.

||Sakhi||

_kabir nav man sut arujhijhya, kabira ghar ghar dwar,
tahan surujhaya bapra (ramji), jahan jani bhakti murari ||1||
kabir balihari guru apna, arujhjhaya sarujhjhod,
nav man sut arujhijhya, so palme kiya nimed ||2||_
(Kabir: nine maunds of thread got entangled, in house after house, at door after door; there it was untangled, poor thing, by Ram, where devotion to Murari became known. Kabir: great is my own guru, who took what was entangled and untangled it — the nine maunds of tangled thread he resolved in a single moment.)

Das Kabirji says: by forgetting the original, true reality, every embodied soul becomes entangled, in the dealings of the body, in nine maunds of thread — the four inner faculties [mind, intellect, chitta, and ego] and the five sense-organs [of sound, touch, form, taste, and smell]. There, whoever was thus helplessly entangled had their confusion untied by God, the Guru, at the point where devotion to Murari-Hari became known to them.

Das Kabirji says: great is the grace of our guru, who untied the tangle in which a body bound by nine maunds of thread-like entanglement — the four inner faculties and five sense-organs — was caught, and who resolved and settled it in a single instant. (Kam Pustakalay No. 393, p. 55.)

On the soul, the Nyaya school's view (Vichar Sagar, page 461): the Nyaya doctrine holds that [1.] pleasure, [2.] pain, 3. knowledge, 4. desire, 5. aversion, 6. effort, 7. dharma (merit), 8. adharma (demerit), 9. mental impressions (samskaras) of knowledge, 10. number, 11. change/result, 12. distinctness, 13. conjunction, and 14. disjunction — these fourteen qualities pertain to the soul (jiva) as atma. (No., Ne. 1, p. 50 — see note.) An attempt has been made, as above, in the Vichar Sagar, to reckon how many difficulties the individual soul (jivatma) runs into by exercising the intellect.

||Kafi||
_nahi vako varpar, saheb nyara hai,
jo kahiye so nahi tahi, aisa akal pasara hai ||tek||
nahi jiv shiv bhi nahi, nahi purush aur nar,
nahi nirgun nahi (nirakar) akar ||1||
nahi lekh alekh bhi nahi, nahi ko akar,
rajot sarup vahi te nyara, soi sarjanhar ||2||
nahi sthul sukshm bhi nahi, nahi rup arup ||3||
aave na jay mare na jive, nahi gam aur tham,
kahat kabir suno bhai santo, aisa hai so ram ||4||_
(There is no end to him; the Lord is unlike anything else — whatever you say of him, he is not that; such is his ungraspable extent. He is not the soul, nor Shiva; not male, not female; not Nirguna, not formless, not possessed of form. He is not written, nor unwritten; he has no shape at all; his form of splendor is beyond even that — he alone is the creator. He is not gross, nor subtle; not with form, nor without form. He neither comes nor goes, neither dies nor lives; he has no village, no place. Kabir says: listen, brother saints, such wondrous is that Ram.)

Das Kabirji says: the divine reality has no end; that Lord is unlike anything else. Whatever you might say of him, he is not really that — such is his inconceivable, ungraspable extent. He is not the soul-principle (jiva), nor formless, nor possessing form; nor is he female. He is neither Nirguna nor formless nor possessed of form. He is neither visible nor invisible, nor does he have any shape. His form of light is beyond even that; he alone is the creator of creation. He is neither vastly great nor minutely small; neither possessing form nor without form. He neither comes nor goes, neither dies nor lives. For him there is no village or place. Das Kabirji says: O saints, listen — such is the wondrous nature of that Ram.

A pure mind: _ulajhanoko sulajhaneke liye aur dharm sankat upasthit hone par samuchit vyavastha deneke liye parishkrit (safe karelu) aur nirmal mastishk ki avashyakta hai_ (to untangle confusions, and to give the proper resolution when a dilemma of dharma arises, a refined and pure mind is needed). — Najar, No. 1, p. 25.

_ghar sutarne fadke, ghani gunjavan vir,
tani tode akalo, dhire ukele dhir_
(In the household — a ball of thread — many knots arise, brother; the impatient one tugs and breaks the tangle, while the patient one slowly unravels it.) — Register 231, pp. 1939 and 2144.

A household is like a ball of the thread of worldly existence: however many knots arise in the life of a householder struggling in the world, when it comes to untangling them, one who grows impatient and angry simply breaks off the knotted part, while a person of calm nature slowly and patiently unravels it.

Keeping silence is best. Between husband and wife, parents and children, brothers and sisters, and other such close relations, wherever there is a close bond, if one of the two becomes harsh, the other must become gentle. If, instead of staying calm, the other also grows heated and starts flinging harsh words, it is like pouring ghee onto fire. In such a conflagration all one's close relatives get burned up, while others merely get a spectacle to watch. Enemies gain the pleasure of gloating over it without even trying. Even one's own work cannot be done properly because of the mind's agitation. Excess cleverness will only create confusion in matters of true, ultimate welfare (paramartha) — that is exactly why it is said: _nav man sut ulajhiya, ghar ghar bar_ (nine maunds of thread got entangled, in house after house, at door after door).

In this chapter, "The Brahma of the World (Maya)," by showing the divine reality that carried off the Brahmin children of Dwarka, and Shri Krishna, who brought those children back, an attempt has been made to clarify the matter of the original, true Supreme Being, the Parabrahma. The followers of the path of ritual action (karma-margis) have tried to understand, by means of twelve names, the Lord of the cosmic egg who carried off those children. The Parabrahma Paramatma is of the nature of light (jyoti swaroop) — that is the original, true light of God, whom even one such as Parvati is unable to see; and the light that people try to know as the Supreme Being through twelve names is, in fact, the light of the Maya-Brahma form. In this way a confusion has arisen between the true Brahma-reality and the illusory (mayavi) Brahma-reality. Through this chapter the Samagam has made known the very twelve names by which those who try to know God through twelve names have themselves created this confusion. Such confusion has also been created by the Vedas, and it has come about through great pronouncements (mahavakyas) such as _aham brahma_, _prajnanam brahma_, and the like; and the Vedas, growing weary, stop short by saying "neti [not this, not this]." The Brahmanical scriptures and the Upanishads too have struggled to understand Brahma, but no conclusion has been reached. Japa, tapa, vows, pilgrimage, and the like have led people into error in this world.

Having held this Samagam at Shahapur, the true dharma of Vaishnav devotion was shown to all Vaishnavs; devoted Vaishnavs of one's own household were called into refuge, the Vaishnav dharma was set going among them, and they were led to attain the supreme benefit.
